generatedAtTimeString and generatedCodesString are read from the form and may be null if the hidden fields are omitted. The tamper check calls equals on these values, so a malformed or tampered required-action submission causes a NullPointerException instead of re-challenging the user.

true_positives.golden_comment: Need to add changelog/release notes documenting the exit code change and migration guidance
true_positives.matched_candidate:
CLI exit code for recreate changed and 4 repurposed

The PR changes RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE from 4 to 3 and introduces FEATURE_DISABLED=4. Any automation written against the previous runtime behavior, where exit code 4 meant a recreate upgrade was required, may now misinterpret exit code 4 as feature-disabled and may miss the recreate result signaled by exit code 3. Since the guide documents these exit codes as a scripting contract, this change is a backward-incompatible CLI contract change and should be explicitly validated and called out.
true_positives.reasoning: The golden comment asks for changelog or release notes that document the exit code change and give migration guidance. The candidate identifies the same exit code change as backward-incompatible and says it should be "explicitly called out", which implies documenting it for users. The underlying concern is the same: users need to be informed of the breaking change. The candidate's emphasis is on the compatibility risk rather than specifically on changelog or release notes, so the match is not exact.

false_positives.candidate:
Exit-code contract for the new feature gate is not tested

The PR adds exit code 4 for the disabled rolling-updates feature and changes the recreate exit code to 3, but the distribution tests only assert log messages. testFeatureNotEnabled asserts the error string but does not assert exit code 4, testWrongVersions does not assert exit code 3, and only the metadata subcommand is exercised for the disabled-feature path. Because the documentation presents these exit codes as a scriptable contract, regressions in the exit-code behavior would not be caught.

Enabled features are overwritten instead of appended

createInitialDeployment calls setEnabledFeatures(List.of(Profile.Feature.ROLLING_UPDATES.getKey())), which replaces any already-configured enabled features in the FeatureSpec. If the shared test fixture or future test setup enables other features, this helper will silently disable them. It should add rolling-updates to the existing enabled-feature list rather than overwrite the list.

true_positives.golden_comment: In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, the method getResourceTypeResource could return null, leading to a NullPointerException in findByResource. Defensive null checks are needed to prevent this issue.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Null type resource causes NullPointerException in client permission check

In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel, String), AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...) can return null when the realm does not support the admin authorization schema or when the Clients type resource has not been created. The following call authz.getStoreFactory().getPolicyStore().findByResource(server, resource) does not check for null, so the permission check throws NullPointerException instead of returning false.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments describe the same issue. In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, getResourceTypeResource can return null, and passing that null to findByResource causes a NullPointerException because there is no null check.

false_positives.candidate:
Client-specific permission check does not fall back to all-clients permission when a resource already exists

In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel, String), the all-clients type resource is consulted only when no resource named after the client's ID exists. If a client-specific resource exists (for example because another scope was granted or a resource was left behind), the method evaluates only that resource. A valid permission on the Clients type resource is then ignored for the requested scope, so an administrator who has an all-clients permission can be denied for that client.

Provider event listener can invoke unsupported V2 setPermissionsEnabled

registerListener executes cleanup only when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is enabled. However management() returns MgmtPermissionsV2 whenever ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled. If both features are enabled, removal events call V2 implementations such as ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled, which throw UnsupportedOperationException. This can break provider event processing or leave old permission data uncleared. The listener should be skipped when V2 is active or should explicitly use the V1 management implementation.

getScope can NPE for missing or unknown resource type

In AdminPermissionsSchema.getScope, when the authorization schema is supported, the code dereferences SCHEMA.getResourceTypes().get(resourceType).getScopes() without verifying that the map lookup returned a ResourceType. A null or unknown resource type causes a NullPointerException (HTTP 500) rather than a ModelValidationException.

Existing admin-permissions clients are not upgraded with Clients scopes/resources

AdminPermissionsSchema.init() returns immediately if realm.getAdminPermissionsClient() is not null. Realms that were initialized before this change therefore do not get the new client scopes (configure, map-roles-client-scope, map-roles-composite) or the Clients all-resource. Existing deployments can then fail scope lookups or evaluate client permissions incorrectly after upgrade.

getResourceName does not resolve client resources

AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceName only special-cases Users. For Clients resources it falls back to resource.getDisplayName(), but client resources are created with the client's UUID as the resource name and no display name. As a result, client permissions/resources may be represented with null or raw UUID names instead of a readable client identifier or 'All clients'.

Missing coverage for all-clients permission when a client-specific resource exists

The new tests exercise single-client permissions and all-client permissions separately, but do not test the case where a client-specific authorization resource already exists and an all-clients permission should still grant access. That scenario covers the fallback logic in ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission and would catch regressions where all-clients permissions are ignored once a specific resource exists.

This is inconsistent with other methods in the class that use ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2. Consequently, if ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled but V1 is not, the permission cleanup logic will not execute, leading to orphaned permission data. Cleanup should occur regardless of which fine-grained authorization version is enabled.

true_positives.golden_comment: In GroupPermissionsV2.canManage(), the permission fallback checks for both VIEW and MANAGE scopes (hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)), but canManage() should only grant access for MANAGE scope, not VIEW. The canView() method correctly checks both VIEW and MANAGE, but canManage() should only check MANAGE.

true_positives.reasoning: Both comments describe the same bug. GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() checks VIEW as well as MANAGE, so users with only VIEW permission get manage access. Both say the check should require only MANAGE.

true_positives.golden_comment: In getGroupIdsWithViewPermission, hasPermission is called with groupResource.getId() and the same groupResource.getId() is added to granted, but hasPermission resolves resources by name (treating the argument as a group id) and the GroupPermissionEvaluator contract says this method returns group IDs that are later used as UserModel.GROUPS and in getUsersCount group filters. true_positives.matched_candidate:
getGroupIdsWithViewPermission uses authorization resource IDs instead of group IDs

In GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission(), the code calls hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...) and adds groupResource.getId() to the returned set. hasPermission expects a realm group ID because it looks up the authorization resource by name, and callers such as UsersResource put the returned set into UserModel.GROUPS to filter user searches by group membership. Both also note the downstream impact on UserModel.GROUPS filtering and on counts.

false_positives.candidate:
Per-instance authorization resources are created without a resource type

AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource() creates authorization resources for individual clients, groups, and users but never calls resource.setType(resourceType). Only the type-level resources created during init() have a type. Consequently type-based lookups such as resourceStore.findByType(server, GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...) in GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission cannot find instance resources, breaking enumeration of groups with permissions.

No migration of scopes/resources for existing admin-permissions clients

AdminPermissionsSchema.init() returns immediately if realm.getAdminPermissionsClient() is already present. Existing realms that initialized V2 before this change will not receive the new Groups scopes or the Groups type resource. Subsequent use of group permissions can fail with missing scopes or null type resources. Initialization should idempotently add missing scopes/resources to existing admin-permissions clients.

Provider event cleanup is incompatible with V2 group permissions

On GroupRemovedEvent the listener calls management(...).groups().setPermissionsEnabled(group, false). When ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled, management() returns MgmtPermissionsV2 and groups() returns GroupPermissionsV2, whose setPermissionsEnabled throws UnsupportedOperationException. This can cause group deletion failures or swallowed errors. If the V1 feature is disabled, the listener is not registered at all and V2 authorization resources may be orphaned. A V2-aware cleanup path is needed.

getScope can throw NullPointerException for unknown or missing resource type

AdminPermissionsSchema.getScope() validates schema scopes with SCHEMA.getResourceTypes().get(resourceType).getScopes() without checking whether resourceType is null or whether the map lookup returns null. Invalid or missing resource types will cause a NullPointerException instead of a ModelValidationException.

Fallback to all-groups resource can NPE if the type resource is missing

GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission() falls back to AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...) and then calls policyStore.findByResource(server, resource). getResourceTypeResource can return null if the Groups type resource was not initialized, leading to a NullPointerException. The same pattern exists in UserPermissionsV2.hasPermission. The code should handle a missing type resource gracefully.

getResourceName does not handle the new Groups resource type

AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceName() only special-cases Users resources. For Groups resources it falls back to resource.getDisplayName(), but group instance resources are created with the group ID as the name and no display name. Administrative UI or policy representations may therefore show blank names for group resources.

The Javadoc for requireManageMembers says it throws ForbiddenException if canManageMembership(GroupModel) returns false, but implementations check canManageMembers(GroupModel). The same interface also documents getGroupIdsWithViewPermission as returning a Stream while the method returns a Set.

true_positives.golden_comment: When length starts at -1 from indefinite-length encoding, the arithmetic 'length = length - bytes.length' will behave unexpectedly, potentially leading to incorrect processing of encoded data.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Indefinite-length ASN.1 values are not handled safely

readLength returns -1 for indefinite-length encoding, but callers do not support this value. readSequence will silently stop parsing, while readInteger/readNext can end up passing a negative or otherwise invalid length to read(int), causing NegativeArraySizeException or reading incorrect bytes. Malformed ASN.1 input should be rejected with IOException rather than causing undefined behavior.
true_positives.reasoning: Both describe the same problem: the -1 returned for indefinite-length encoding is used in later length handling. The golden comment points to the arithmetic in the sequence loop. The candidate notes that readSequence silently stops parsing and that other callers misuse the negative length. That is the same underlying bug.

true_positives.golden_comment: Abstract order() method on CryptoProvider may break backward compatibility with existing implementations
true_positives.matched_candidate:
New order() method breaks existing CryptoProvider implementations

CryptoProvider is loaded via ServiceLoader and can be implemented outside this repository. Adding `int order()` as a non-default interface method breaks source and binary compatibility for existing providers: older implementations will fail to compile against the new API and may throw AbstractMethodError at runtime when CryptoIntegration sorts them. A default method should be provided instead.
true_positives.reasoning: Both point to the same problem: adding a non-default abstract order() method to the CryptoProvider interface breaks backward compatibility for existing implementations.

false_positives.candidate:
Multiple providers with equal order are selected silently and non-deterministically

detectProvider now loads all registered CryptoProviders, sorts them by order descending, and returns the first one. All full providers in this PR return the same order (200), so if more than one real provider is present (for example default and FIPS/Elytron), the selected provider depends on ServiceLoader/classpath ordering. The previous fail-fast behavior was removed and ignored providers are only debug-logged. This can silently select an unintended crypto provider, with security-sensitive consequences. Consider failing on ties for the highest order, or at least logging a warning and assigning distinct orders.

Zero-length INTEGER causes NumberFormatException instead of IOException

readInteger reads the length and then constructs a BigInteger from the read bytes. If a malformed DER INTEGER has length 0, `new BigInteger(bytes)` throws NumberFormatException, an unchecked exception, instead of the IOException used for other ASN.1 parsing failures. The parser should validate that the integer length is positive and throw IOException for malformed input.

integerToBytes silently discards leading bytes of oversized coordinates

In the ECDSA conversion, when BigInteger.toByteArray() returns more bytes than the expected coordinate length, integerToBytes copies only the last qLength bytes without verifying that the discarded leading bytes are zero. A valid positive integer may be one byte longer due to a DER sign byte, but a larger or corrupted value will be silently truncated, producing an incorrect concatenated R/S signature. The method should reject oversized values or verify that all dropped bytes are zero.

ECDSA tests do not use algorithm-appropriate curves or verify signatures

The test generates a default EC key pair and uses it for ES256, ES384, and ES512, so the larger algorithms are not exercised with their expected curves or key sizes. It also only checks that concatenated R/S values round-trip through the converter; it never verifies that the DER-encoded signature produced by concatenatedRSToASN1DER is accepted by Signature.verify, nor does it cover edge cases such as coordinates with leading zeros or the high bit set. Add curve-specific key generation and signature verification tests.

true_positives.golden_comment: The reader thread isn’t waited for; flipping deletedAll to true and asserting immediately can race and miss exceptions added just after the flag change, making this test flaky.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Concurrency test does not wait for the reader thread and can miss failures

The test starts a background thread that records exceptions, then deletes groups, sets deletedAll, and immediately asserts that caughtExceptions is empty. The test also does not verify that any read actually overlapped with the deletes. If the delete loop throws, deletedAll may never be set, leaving the reader thread running after the test. false_positives.candidate:

New messages then cannot be processed, and enqueue attempts may fail or be dropped. The pool lifecycle must match the strategy lifecycle, or the pool must be recreated on each assignment.

false_positives.candidate:

In Create, and similarly in Delete, Update, and DeleteCollection, the background goroutine creates a timeout context from the incoming request context. Request contexts are normally canceled when the HTTP handler returns, so the 10-second timeout does not make the legacy write independent. The legacy operation may be canceled immediately after the API response is sent, causing mode 3 to skip the intended asynchronous legacy write. A detached context, with logger/values copied, should be used instead.

Mode3.Create passes the original obj to Legacy.Create after Storage.Create has returned created. Storage may assign name, UID, resourceVersion, annotations, or defaults, and created is the canonical object that unified storage accepted. Passing the original object, rather than a deep copy of created, can create a different object in legacy storage or cause concurrent use of a mutable object. This can make legacy storage diverge from unified storage.

Legacy Update reuses the request UpdatedObjectInfo instead of the unified result

Mode3.Update calls Storage.Update with objInfo and then asynchronously calls Legacy.Update with the same objInfo. Legacy.Update will normally evaluate objInfo against the legacy store's current object, so patches, strategic merges, or resource-version-dependent updates can produce a different result or fail. To keep legacy consistent, the legacy update should receive an UpdatedObjectInfo that returns the exact object returned by Storage.Update, preferably a deep copy.

Unordered background goroutines can leave legacy storage inconsistent

Each write operation starts an independent goroutine to write to legacy storage without sequencing, queueing, or per-resource locking. Rapid create/update/delete operations can be applied to legacy out of order, for example a legacy delete can run before a legacy create or an older update can overwrite a newer one. Because mode 3 keeps legacy as a fallback, this can resurrect deleted objects or leave stale data if legacy is later used.

Delete does not attempt legacy deletion when unified delete returns NotFound

DualWriterMode3.Delete returns immediately on any Storage.Delete error, including NotFound. The previous behavior tolerated NotFound from unified storage and still attempted to delete from legacy storage. With the new behavior, objects that are already absent from unified storage but still present in legacy cannot be cleaned through the API, leaving orphaned legacy data.

When Storage.Create fails, recordLegacyDuration is called at line 45; when Storage.Update fails, recordLegacyDuration is called at line 129; and the asynchronous Legacy.DeleteCollection result is recorded with recordStorageDuration at line 166. These record the duration or error state of the wrong store, making mode 3 observability misleading.

Background legacy writes are detached and untracked

Mode 3 launches a new goroutine for every write with no wait group, queue, or shutdown coordination. Destroy can close Storage and Legacy while background writes are still running, which may cause failures or panics if the underlying stores are closed. There is also no backpressure, so a slow legacy backend can cause unbounded goroutine growth.

Asynchronous legacy write failures are not logged

The background create, update, delete, and delete-collection paths only record a metric when the legacy operation fails. They do not log the error or cause. Because these writes are asynchronous and can fail due to cancellation, timeouts, conflicts, or backend errors, operators will have no actionable logs to diagnose legacy divergence.

Mode 3 unit tests do not synchronize or set expectations for async legacy calls

For the cache TTL, subsequent requests with the same device ID hit the cache and TagDevice returns nil without touching the database, so Anonymous.Authenticate succeeds. A device that was initially rejected by the device limit can therefore retry and bypass the limit, and database failures are also hidden.

Because the device ID header is supplied by the client, an anonymous client can omit it and avoid being counted or blocked, while normal UI clients that send the header are limited. TopicEmbed.import creates posts with skip_validations and cook_method Post.cook_methods[:raw_html], so Post#cook returns the imported feed/readability HTML unchanged. The embed view renders post.cooked with raw. Untrusted RSS/Atom or scraped content can therefore contain script tags, event handlers, or javascript: URLs, leading to stored XSS in Discourse and embedding pages.

EmbedController#best only validates the Referer host, then enqueues :retrieve_topic for any embed_url parameter. The embed_url host is only checked later inside TopicRetriever. This allows a client that can present an acceptable Referer to enqueue many jobs for arbitrary URLs, causing Sidekiq load and unwanted fetch attempts. Validate and/or throttle embed_url before enqueuing.

SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) uses open-uri without timeouts, redirect controls, or rescue for network and parse errors. A slow, unreachable, or malformed feed can hang or crash the scheduled job.

retrieved_recently? calls $redis.setnx and then $redis.expire. If the process crashes between those calls, or expire fails, the key remains without a TTL and that embed URL can be throttled forever. Use an atomic SET with NX and EX, or another safe Redis pattern.

perform_retrieve executes Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({}) inline whenever a single unknown embed URL is requested and feed polling is enabled. Each distinct unknown URL can force a complete fetch and import of the configured feed, which is expensive and can be abused. The feed poll should be debounced or enqueued asynchronously.

In the update branch, TopicEmbed.import calls PostRevisor#revise! and then unconditionally updates the embed content_sha1. If the revision/save fails or returns false, the stored SHA will no longer match the post body and future legitimate content changes may be skipped.

Post creation success is checked with present? instead of persisted?

After PostCreator#create, TopicEmbed.import checks if post.present?. PostCreator can return an unsaved Post object with errors after a rollback, so this condition can be true for a non-persisted post. The subsequent TopicEmbed.create! can then fail on nil topic_id/post_id or create inconsistent data. Check post.persisted? and errors before creating the embed.

TopicEmbed belongs_to :topic and :post but has no dependent destroy or cleanup callback. If a topic or post is destroyed, stale topic_embed rows remain. topic_id_for_embed can then return a deleted topic id, and update code may later call methods on a nil post.

PostCreator jobs are enqueued inside the outer Topic.transaction

TopicEmbed.import wraps PostCreator#create in a Topic.transaction. PostCreator enqueues background jobs after its own Post.transaction block, but that block is nested inside the outer transaction, so jobs may be queued before the topic/embed data is committed. Workers can race and fail to see the new records.

TopicEmbed.import_remote calls open(url).read without timeouts or error handling. A slow or failing remote host can hang the retrieve-topic worker. This fetch should use explicit timeouts and rescue network errors.

absolutize_urls omits the port whenever it is 80 or 443, regardless of URI scheme. For http://host:443/ or https://host:80/, it will generate URLs without the required port. Compare the port against the default port for the URI scheme instead.

The embed/best view calls post.user.small_avatar_url and post.user.username without nil checks. Posts can have missing or deleted users, which will cause a NoMethodError when rendering the embedded topic.

Changing this migration to create_table :top_topics, force: true means the migration will drop the top_topics table if it already exists. If this migration is rerun or run against a database where the table was created previously, data can be lost. Use a new migration or conditional DDL instead.

false_positives.candidate:

The `unsubscribe` action changes the user's `TopicUser.notification_level` while being served by GET routes (`t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe` and `t/:topic_id/unsubscribe`). Because the new level depends on the current level, repeated or prefetched requests can silently change the subscription (for example watching -> regular -> muted). State-changing operations should require POST/PUT or a confirmation/token rather than occur on page load.

The endpoint downgrades tracking/watching topics to `regular` instead of `muted`. If the feature is meant to stop notifications for that topic, set the level to muted or make the desired target level explicit.

Instead of using `TopicUser.change`, the action updates the row with `save!`. `TopicUser.change` is the established path for notification-level changes: it sets `notifications_changed_at` and `notifications_reason_id` and publishes a MessageBus notification-level change. Use a separate key, provide a safe default, or make the topic-specific line conditional.

No controller/request specs were added for the new unsubscribe endpoint. Tests are needed for successful notification-level changes, missing TopicUser rows, unauthorized or private topics, slug redirects, JSON versus HTML responses, and repeated GET requests.

false_positives.candidate:
Delete-cache mutation does not invalidate connected calendars query

After `deleteCacheMutation` succeeds, the component only calls `onSuccess`. It does not invalidate `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` (unlike the disconnect mutation). In `SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper`, `onChanged` is optional and may not refetch the query, so the cache status/timestamp can remain visible after the cache rows are deleted. Invalidate the connectedCalendars query or update its cache in `onSettled`.

Cache status query includes expired cache entries

`getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` groups all `CalendarCache` rows for the credentials but does not filter `expiresAt >= now()`, while cache reads (`getCachedAvailability`) only use unexpired rows. The UI can therefore show a cache status and allow deleting cache data that is already expired and not being served. Filter by `expiresAt` if the status is meant to represent active cache.

updateManyByCredentialId accepts relation-update input not supported by updateMany

`updateManyByCredentialId` types `data` as `Prisma.SelectedCalendarUpdateInput`, which includes relation operations such as connect/disconnect. `prisma.selectedCalendar.updateMany` only supports scalar update-many inputs, so the repository signature can accept payloads that will fail at runtime. Use `Prisma.SelectedCalendarUpdateManyMutationInput` or `Prisma.SelectedCalendarUncheckedUpdateManyInput`.

Actions container renders empty space when dropdown is hidden

`CredentialActionsDropdown` returns `null` when there is no cache action and no disconnect action, but it is wrapped in a fixed-width `<div className="flex w-32 justify-end">`. This leaves an empty 8rem action area in list cards/alerts for delegation credentials or when modifications are disabled. Render the wrapper conditionally or move the width styling into the dropdown component.

credentialId validation allows non-integer numbers

The `deleteCache` input validates `credentialId` only as `z.number()`. Credential IDs are integers; accepting floats can pass validation and then produce unexpected Prisma behavior. Use `z.number().int()`.

Existing CalendarCache rows are backfilled with migration timestamp

Adding `updatedAt` with `DEFAULT NOW()` sets every existing cache row to the deployment/migration time. The new UI will show legacy cache entries as recently updated even though their contents may be much older. If accurate status matters, backfill from a meaningful timestamp or treat pre-existing rows specially.

dev:cron uses npx tsx without declaring tsx dependency

The script changed from `ts-node` to `npx tsx`, but `tsx` is not listed as a devDependency. `npx` may prompt to download the package or fail in offline/CI environments. Add `tsx` to devDependencies or keep an already-installed runner.

ENV_FILE path is relative to current working directory

`ENV_FILE="../.env"` depends on where the script is executed. Running `scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh` from the repository root will target the parent directory of the repo, not the repo root. Resolve the path relative to the script location (e.g. `$(dirname "$0")/../.env`).

true_positives.reasoning: Both comments flag the same bug: dayjs objects are compared with ===, which checks reference identity and so is always false. Both recommend using isSame() instead.

false_positives.candidate:
Date override availability skips busy-time check

In checkIfIsAvailable, when dateOverrideExist is true and the slot is not rejected by the date-override predicate, the function returns true before executing the busy.every check. This means any busy time from bookings, calendars, or other sources is ignored for slots covered by a date override. A host who is already busy can still be shown as available, which can lead to invalid slot offers and double-booking risks.

Working-hours check rejects slots if any interval does not contain them

workingHours.find is used as if it detects whether a slot is outside working hours, but the callback returns true whenever the slot is outside the current working-hour interval. If a user has multiple working-hour intervals in one day, a slot inside one interval will be outside another interval and the whole check returns false, hiding valid availability. Conversely, if there is no working-hour entry for that weekday, the check falls through and treats the slot as available. The logic should require that at least one working-hour interval fully contains the slot.

Date-override containment allows partially overlapping slots

The date-override check only rejects slots that end before or exactly at the override start, or start after the override end. It does not reject slots that start before the override start or end after the override end. It also treats a slot starting exactly at the override end as valid because isAfter is used instead of an isSame-or-after boundary check. Therefore, slots that only partially overlap a date override can pass availability.

Multiple date overrides for the same day are not handled correctly

The dateOverrides.find callback sets dateOverrideExist as a side effect and returns true for the first override that the slot is outside. If a user has two date overrides on the same date, a slot inside the second override can be rejected because it is outside the first override, and find stops at that first rejection. Availability with multiple per-day overrides will be incorrect.

getSlots now relies on optional timeZone being populated

TimeRange.timeZone was added as an optional field, but getSlots now calls dayjs(...).tz(override.timeZone) unconditionally. Only the trpc slots router was updated to populate timeZone on date overrides. Other callers of getSlots that pass DateOverride objects without timeZone may get invalid timezone handling, incorrect slots, or runtime failures. The type should make this requirement explicit or the code should safely fall back.

Timezone-converted overrides can lose cross-midnight information

Override start and end times are converted to minutes using hour() * 60 + minute() after applying a timezone offset. If the timezone conversion moves an override across local midnight, the date portion is discarded. endTime can become numerically smaller than startTime, causing buildSlots to skip the range, or the override can be attached to the wrong invitee day. This makes late-night overrides unreliable for invitees in different timezones.

No automated test for the fixed-host round-robin date override fix

The added test only checks a personal event date override in a different invitee timezone. The PR's primary stated fix is that fixed hosts' date overrides must constrain round-robin availability, but there is no test with a round-robin event, a fixed host, and a date override. There is also no test that busy times still block slots inside date overrides. This leaves the main behavior and the critical busy-time interaction untested.

fixedHosts is recomputed for every slot

Inside timeSlots.filter, fixedHosts = userAvailability.filter(...) is computed for every slot. The set of fixed hosts does not change during the request. Hoisting this computation outside the slot filter avoids repeated O(number_of_slots * number_of_users) filtering.

typeof result compared to undefined instead of a string

The condition typeof availabilityCheckProps.currentSeats !== undefined is always true because typeof returns a string, and the later condition typeof availabilityCheckProps.currentSeats === undefined is always false. If currentSeats is undefined while occupied seats exist, the code can call map or push on undefined and crash. The checks should compare against the string 'undefined' or use availabilityCheckProps.currentSeats !== undefined directly.

false_positives.candidate:
Returned SQL condition is not always parenthesized and can compose incorrectly

getAuthorizationConditions can return an OR predicate for org/team scope, and getBaseConditions returns that auth condition unwrapped when there are no filters. If a caller adds more predicates, e.g. `WHERE ${baseConditions} AND startTime > x`, SQL operator precedence makes the extra predicate apply only to one side of the OR, potentially returning rows that should be filtered out. The service should return a fully parenthesized predicate, or wrap the final result in getBaseConditions, so the fragment is safe to embed alongside other conditions.

Public options type makes teamId optional for team scope

The previous discriminated union type would have caught the missing `teamId` at compile time. Use a discriminated public type or surface validation errors.

Exact SQL equality assertions depend on unordered repository result order

The org-scope test asserts exact Prisma.sql equality with arrays of team and user IDs in a specific order, but the service builds those arrays from repository queries without explicit ordering. The SQL semantics are unaffected by order, but the assertion can fail nondeterministically if rows are returned in a different order. Sort IDs in the service or compare normalized sets.

Breaking service API change without caller migration in this PR

The class removes the previous public `findMany` method and changes condition methods to return `Prisma.Sql` instead of Prisma where inputs. This is a breaking contract change for any existing caller of the service. If callers are expected to compose raw SQL now, they should be updated in this PR or the old API should be retained/deprecated.

true_positives.golden_comment: The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.

true_positives.reasoning: The candidate names the same function, appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse, and describes the same failure: throwing on invalid payloads produces a 500 instead of a 400. It also mentions other functions that can throw, but the core issue is the same.

false_positives.candidate:
Webhook secret is compared with ===

The endpoint authenticates requests by comparing the incoming header to process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET using JavaScript equality. String equality can short-circuit and may be vulnerable to timing analysis, allowing an attacker to gradually infer the secret. Use crypto.timingSafeEqual on fixed-length buffers after verifying both values exist.

Credential upsert is not atomic and can create duplicates

The handler searches for an existing credential with findFirst and then creates or updates it in separate queries. There is no transaction or unique constraint on (userId, appId). Concurrent webhook deliveries for the same user/app can both miss an existing row and insert duplicates, or if duplicates already exist findFirst may update an arbitrary row. This can leave users with multiple/stale credentials and app adapters may use the wrong one.

Webhook accepts all HTTP methods

The API route does not check req.method, so any HTTP method is processed. It should only accept POST, or the documented method, and return 405 for others.

parseRefreshTokenResponse throws despite callers expecting safeParse result

The helper calls safeParse but then throws an Error when validation fails, while several callers still check .success to handle invalid tokens gracefully. This changes the contract and turns recoverable invalid-token responses into unhandled exceptions or bypasses intended error handling in apps such as Zoom and Salesforce.

prisma is used but never imported

The new token-refresh code calls prisma.credential.update, but the file does not import prisma from @calcom/prisma. This will cause a ReferenceError at runtime, and likely a TypeScript/build error, whenever Salesforce credential refresh is attempted.

Salesforce client refreshes token on every instantiation

getClient performs an OAuth token refresh every time a SalesforceCalendarService is constructed, regardless of whether the existing access token is still valid. Calendar operations instantiate services frequently, which can cause unnecessary calls to Salesforce, rate limiting, and increased latency. The token expiry should be checked before refreshing.

Zoho CRM token validity check is inverted

isTokenValid treats expiryDate < Date.now() as valid, which is true only after the token has expired. getToken resolves without refreshing when isTokenValid is true and refreshes when it is false, so expired tokens are used and unexpired tokens trigger refreshes. The expiry is also set using Date.now() + 60 * 60, which is only a few seconds in milliseconds, making the problem worse.

Credential sync request has no authentication or signature

The POST to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT only sends calcomUserId and appSlug; it does not include a shared secret, signature, or other authentication. If the sync endpoint is reachable, it may be possible to request or rotate tokens based on unauthenticated requests. Add a configurable secret/signature header and verify it on the external app store.

No automated tests for privileged credential-sync webhook

The PR introduces a webhook that can create or update arbitrary user credentials, plus multiple token-refresh code paths, but no tests are included. At minimum, tests should cover secret verification, disabled feature behavior, malformed or undecryptable payloads, duplicate credential handling, and sync-enabled refresh flows.

In reschedule flows this leaves stale scheduled reminder rows. true_positives.reasoning: The candidate describes the same problem as the golden comment. In the immediateDelete branch, the function cancels the SendGrid email but neither deletes the WorkflowReminder DB row nor marks it cancelled, which leaves stale or orphaned rows. The candidate does not mention the omitted SendGrid DELETE call, but the core issue is the same.

false_positives.candidate:
Reschedule endpoint does not await old reminder cancellations

In requestReschedule, bookingToReschedule.workflowReminders.forEach calls async deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder without awaiting them. The tRPC mutation can complete before the old booking's reminders are actually marked cancelled/deleted or canceled with the provider, so old reminders may still be delivered.

Rescheduled booking reminder cancellation is fire-and-forget and bypasses deferred cancel

handleNewBooking cancels the original booking's reminders in a forEach without awaiting the async calls, so the surrounding try/catch cannot catch failures and the request may finish before cancellation completes. It also passes immediateDelete=true for email reminders; if the immediate SendGrid cancellation fails, no cancelled flag or DB cleanup is left for retry. Old reminders from a rescheduled booking can therefore still be sent.

Workflow deletion cancels scheduled emails fire-and-forget before cascade delete

In the workflow delete mutation, scheduledReminders.forEach calls deleteScheduledEmailReminder(..., true)/deleteScheduledSMSReminder without awaiting. The workflow is then deleted, cascading away WorkflowReminder rows. If the external SendGrid/Twilio cancellation does not complete or fails, there is no DB state left to retry, and scheduled emails/SMS for the deleted workflow may still be sent.

Cron authentication can pass when CRON_API_KEY is unset

The cron handler compares process.env.CRON_API_KEY with the supplied apiKey using strict inequality. If CRON_API_KEY is not configured, both sides are undefined for a request with no key, so the endpoint is accessible without authentication. This endpoint can cancel and schedule workflow emails, so it should require a configured CRON_API_KEY and reject unauthenticated requests.

Cron cancellation query is too broad and can include rows without a SendGrid batch id

scheduleEmailReminders selects remindersToCancel only by cancelled=true and scheduledDate. It does not filter method=EMAIL, scheduled=true, or referenceId not null. The loop then sends reminder.referenceId as batch_id to SendGrid. A row with a null/invalid referenceId, or a non-email reminder if cancelled is ever set, can make the request fail; due to the surrounding error handling, that can prevent other valid cancellations from being processed.

A single failure aborts the whole cron cancellation loop

The cancellation logic awaits each SendGrid request inside one try/catch around the whole for loop. If any request throws, such as from rate limiting, a network error, or an invalid batch id, control jumps to catch and the remaining reminders are neither canceled in SendGrid nor deleted from WorkflowReminder. Those reminders can still be sent. Each reminder should be canceled with independent error handling.

Cron may schedule stale reminders without checking booking status or cancelled flag

The unscheduledReminders query filters only method=EMAIL, scheduled=false, and scheduledDate. It does not exclude cancelled=true rows and does not require the related booking to still be ACCEPTED. If a reminder row remains after a booking is cancelled/rescheduled, which is possible because cancellation calls are fire-and-forget or can race, the cron will schedule and send an email for that booking.

Paid booking cancellation returns before cancelling workflow reminders

In handleCancelBooking, the paid branch refunds the booking, updates it to REJECTED, and returns before the later code that cancels workflow reminders. Therefore cancelled paid bookings can retain scheduled workflow reminders. Since the PR is intended to stop reminders for cancelled bookings, this early return should also perform the reminder cancellation or move cancellation before the return.

The intended check appears to be admin OR owner, so the endpoint's authorization does not match the variable name and likely product intent.

true_positives.golden_comment: The sendAddGuestsEmails function in email-manager.ts passes the full calendarEvent.attendees array when determining which attendees receive AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, but checks if newGuests.includes(attendee.email) where newGuests is the input guests array.

false_positives.candidate:
Any attendee can modify the guest list

The permission check treats any attendee whose email matches the authenticated user's email as allowed to add guests. This lets a participant, not just the organizer/host, modify the guest list and trigger invitation emails to arbitrary addresses. Unless this is an explicit product decision, the endpoint should restrict this action to hosts/team admins.

Endpoint does not validate booking status

The handler fetches the booking but never checks its status or timing. The API can therefore add guests to cancelled, rejected, pending, or past bookings even if the UI hides the action. This can send notifications and update calendar events for bookings that should no longer be modified.

No limit on number of guest emails

guests is validated only as an array of email strings with no maximum length. An authenticated user can submit a very large array, causing a large createMany operation and mass email sending. Add a reasonable max length.

Organizer lookup can throw for bookings without a user

The organizer lookup uses `booking.userId || 0` with findFirstOrThrow. If a booking has no userId, for example in some team/round-robin cases, this queries user id 0 and throws a Prisma not-found error, producing a 500 instead of handling the missing organizer.

Attendees are persisted before calendar update without a transaction

Attendees are persisted with prisma.booking.update before calling eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees, and the whole operation is not transactional. If the calendar update fails, guests remain attached to the booking while the client receives an error, leaving Cal.com attendees and external calendar attendees inconsistent.

Invalid-email error state is not reset after successful submission

The mutation success handler closes the dialog and resets the email list but does not reset isInvalidEmail. If a previous submission failed validation and a later submission succeeds, reopening the dialog can still show the stale validation error.

Error toast fallback is never used

The error message is built with a template string that is always non-empty, so the fallback to t('unable_to_add_guests') never runs. Users may see a message like `undefined: ...` when no TRPC error code is present.

To address can be malformed for guests with empty name

New guest attendees are created with an empty name, and the email sets `to` to `${attendee.name} <${attendee.email}>`. This can produce a malformed display name such as ` <guest@example.com>`. Use the email address as a fallback when name is empty.

Hard-coded English tooltip

The remove-email tooltip content is hard-coded as 'Remove email' instead of using the translation hook, so it will not be localized.

No tests for the new add-guests endpoint

No automated tests are added for the new tRPC endpoint, including its permission logic, duplicate/blacklisted email handling, and email selection. These are security-sensitive paths that would benefit from regression tests.

true_positives.golden_comment: Backup code validation is case-sensitive due to the use of indexOf(). This causes validation to fail if a user enters uppercase hex characters, as backup codes should be case-insensitive for a better user experience.

Backup-code matching is case- and whitespace-sensitive

Backup codes are generated as lowercase hex strings, but during login they are compared with `indexOf` after only removing dashes. The value is not trimmed or lowercased. A user who enters a valid code in uppercase, which is suggested by the UI placeholder, or with surrounding whitespace will be rejected despite having a valid backup code.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate identifies the same problem: backup codes are compared with indexOf without lowercasing, so a valid code entered in uppercase is rejected. The extra point about whitespace does not change that the core issue matches.

true_positives.golden_comment: Because backupCodes are decrypted and mutated in memory before being written back, two concurrent login requests using the same backupCode could both pass this check and update, so a single backup code may effectively be accepted more than once if used concurrently, weakening the intended one-time-use semantics.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Backup-code single-use guarantee is not atomic

After matching a backup code, the code is invalidated by decrypting the stored array, setting the matched entry to null, and writing it back with a separate `prisma.user.update`. This read-modify-write is not transactional or protected against concurrent updates. Two simultaneous login attempts using the same backup code can both read it as unused and both succeed. Concurrent uses of different codes can also overwrite each other's updates and resurrect a previously used code.
true_positives.reasoning: Both describe the same problem. The backup code is invalidated through a non-atomic read-modify-write, so concurrent logins with the same code can both succeed, breaking one-time use.

false_positives.candidate:
Backup-code login can bypass password verification

In the credentials authorize callback, the password is only verified when `!credentials.totpCode` (line 121). The new backup-code branch at line 131 is entered whenever `credentials.backupCode` is present, even if a non-empty `totpCode` is also supplied. An attacker can send credentials containing any non-empty `totpCode` and a valid backup code; the password check is skipped and the backup code alone authenticates. This turns a backup code into a single-factor credential and allows login without the account password.

Dialog can be dismissed after enabling 2FA without notifying parent or resetting state

After TOTP verification succeeds, the modal switches to the backup-code screen, but `onEnable` and `resetState` are only invoked by the explicit Close button. If the user dismisses the dialog through `onOpenChange` (for example via backdrop click, close icon, or Escape), the parent is not notified that 2FA has been enabled and the modal state is not reset. The settings UI can remain stale until a reload, and sensitive state such as backup codes or object URLs may persist.

Disable endpoint rejects uppercase backup codes

The disable endpoint compares the supplied backup code after removing dashes but without trimming or lowercasing it. Since generated codes are lowercase hex, a valid backup code entered in uppercase or with surrounding whitespace is rejected, preventing a user from disabling 2FA with a valid code.

No tests cover actual backup-code authentication or single-use behavior

The PR adds a security-critical backup-code login and disable flow, but the e2e tests only verify that backup codes can be downloaded, copied, and closed. There is no test that logs in with a backup code, disables 2FA with a backup code, or asserts that a consumed backup code cannot be reused, so the core feature and its single-use guarantee are untested.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The exported function TwoFactor handles backup codes and is in BackupCode.tsx. Inconsistent naming.
Error message mentions 'backup code login' but this is a disable endpoint, not login

Object URL for backup codes is not revoked on component unmount, leading to a potential memory leak. This can cause increased memory usage over time, especially if the component is mounted and unmounted frequently.

The golden comment's framing of when this happens is slightly off, but the candidate correctly identifies the same flawed lookup and its consequence of an undefined calendarId.

The new code sets slug when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true and omits slug when billing is disabled. When EventManager creates events for multiple hosts, each host's credential receives the same full destinationCalendar array, but Lark always tries to use the first host's calendar. The candidate notes that Lark's createEvent ignores the credential and picks the first destination calendar. That points to the same root cause, the missing credentialId in Lark's implementation, but the candidate frames it as a runtime behavior bug rather than an interface contract violation. updateEvent can be called with undefined or stale credential

In updateAllCalendarEvents, when a booking reference has credentialId, the code assigns credential from in-memory credentials or the database. If no credential is found, credential may remain undefined or retain the value from a previous loop iteration, and updateEvent is still pushed. This can cause updates to fail or be attempted with the wrong credential.
true_positives.reasoning: Both point to the same bug: when reference.credentialId is set but no credential is found, updateEvent is still called with an undefined credential. The candidate adds a point about a stale credential, but the core issue is identical.

false_positives.candidate:
TypeError when destinationCalendar is empty and location is Google Meet

In EventManager.create, mainHostDestinationCalendar is destructured from evt.destinationCalendar ?? []. If destinationCalendar is null or an empty array, mainHostDestinationCalendar is undefined, but the next line reads mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration without optional chaining. This will throw a TypeError for Google Meet events that have no destination calendar, breaking booking creation.

Video credentialId is no longer stored in references created by EventManager.create

referencesToCreate now sets credentialId only when the result is a calendar result. Previously, non-calendar results preserved result.credentialId. As a result, video booking references can be created with credentialId undefined. Later cancellation or update flows that look up the video credential by reference.credentialId may fail to delete or update the meeting.

Only the first old calendar reference is deleted when merging bookings

When newBookingId is provided, updateAllCalendarEvents deletes the old calendar event by finding only the first booking reference whose type includes _calendar. For collective or multi-host bookings there can be multiple calendar references, so the remaining old calendar events will not be deleted and can remain on host calendars.

Fallback credential filter looks for exact type calendar

createAllCalendarEvents falls back to this.calendarCredentials.filter(cred => cred.type === 'calendar') when no destinationCalendar is present. Calendar credential types are normally values like google_calendar or office365_calendar, so this exact equality will usually match nothing. The stated fallback to the first connected calendar will therefore not create any calendar event.

Possible duplicate creation for other_calendar integrations

createAllCalendarEvents first creates events for each entry in event.destinationCalendar, then unconditionally creates events for every credential whose type includes other_calendar. If a destinationCalendar entry is itself an other_calendar credential, the same integration event can be created twice.

updateLocation can create booking references without credential or external calendar identifiers

updateLocation maps results into referencesToCreate using result.externalId and result.credentialId. Calendar update results from CalendarManager.updateEvent do not populate these fields, so calendar references produced by updateLocation can have undefined credentialId and externalCalendarId. Handlers that persist these references may store incomplete reference rows.

Team destination calendars are dropped when organizer has no destination calendar

For collective team events, evt.destinationCalendar is initialized to null when neither eventType nor organizer has a destinationCalendar. The later call evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars) then does nothing because of optional chaining on null. Hosts' destination calendars are silently lost, so their calendar events may not be created.

Google deleteEvent fallback can target the wrong calendar

deleteEvent now only uses externalCalendarId when provided; otherwise it attempts to find a destination calendar with externalId === externalCalendarId, which is undefined when no externalCalendarId was passed. It then falls back to primary. If the event exists on a non-primary calendar and externalCalendarId is missing, deletion can fail silently with a 404 or leave the event on the correct calendar.

Google event patch can use undefined calendarId

createEvent inserts the event with calendarId selectedCalendar || 'primary', but the subsequent events.patch call uses calendarId: selectedCalendar without the same fallback. If selectedCalendar is undefined, the patch request can fail even though the event was created on primary.

Google createEvent ignores destination externalId when credentialId is absent

createEvent now chooses the Google calendar by finding a destinationCalendar entry with the same credentialId. Older or incomplete destinationCalendar records may have externalId but no credentialId. In that case the service falls back to primary, whereas the previous behavior could use destinationCalendar.externalId. This can create events on the wrong calendar after the migration to arrays.

Office365 createEvent only uses the first destination calendar for multi-host events

Office365CalendarService.createEvent uses the first entry of event.destinationCalendar and ignores the credentialId passed by CalendarManager. For collective events with multiple destination calendars, every host's credential will attempt to create the event in the first host's calendar, which can fail or produce incorrect events for the other hosts.

CalDAV createEvent only uses the first destination calendar for multi-host events

BaseCalendarService.createEvent filters calendars by the first entry of event.destinationCalendar. It does not select the destination calendar that corresponds to the credential creating the event. With multiple host destination calendars, CalDAV events for non-first hosts can be created on the wrong calendar or fail.

Recurring cancellation only deletes the first calendar reference per booking

When cancelling all remaining recurring bookings, the code finds only the first reference whose type includes _calendar for each updated booking and attempts deletes using the organizer's calendar credentials. Multi-host bookings can have multiple calendar references, including credentials that are not in bookingToDelete.user.credentials, so some host calendar events may not be deleted.

Awaiting the apiDeletes array does not await deletion promises

In the paid cancellation branch, the code executes await apiDeletes where apiDeletes is an array of promises. This does not wait for the promises or catch their rejections. Calendar or video deletions may still be running when the handler returns, and failures will not be handled by the surrounding try/catch.

Confirming a pending collective booking only includes one destination calendar

confirmHandler builds evt.destinationCalendar from only booking.destinationCalendar or user.destinationCalendar. It does not include destination calendars for other collective hosts. When a pending collective booking is confirmed, EventManager.create will therefore only create the organizer's calendar event, not events for all hosts.

Webhook payload destinationCalendar is inconsistent between events

The test expects destinationCalendar to be [] for BOOKING_REJECTED but expects null for BOOKING_CREATED and BOOKING_REQUESTED elsewhere in the same file. The migration to an array-backed destinationCalendar should use a consistent empty representation across webhook payloads to avoid breaking consumers.

false_negatives.golden_comment: A null reference occurs in GoogleCalendarService.createEvent() and updateEvent() when mainHostDestinationCalendar is destructured from evt.destinationCalendar but evt.destinationCalendar is null or an empty array, causing mainHostDestinationCalendar to be undefined.
The optional chaining on mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration is redundant since you already check mainHostDestinationCalendar in the ternary condition.

true_positives.golden_comment: Consider adding try-catch around the await to handle import failures gracefully
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Dynamic import failures in getCalendar reject instead of returning null

getCalendar now awaits appStore[...] but does not catch errors from the dynamic import. Previously an unknown or unavailable calendar type could return null after a warning; now a rejected import throws. Callers such as CalendarManager.getCachedResults use Promise.all over getCalendar, so one broken app can fail all calendar availability requests. Wrap the import lookup in try/catch and return null, or otherwise handle the failure.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments say the awaited dynamic import in getCalendar has no error handling and recommend wrapping it in try/catch so import failures are handled gracefully. That is the same issue.

true_positives.golden_comment: The code uses forEach with async callbacks, which causes asynchronous operations (e.g., calendar/video event deletions, payment refunds) to run concurrently without being awaited. This 'fire-and-forget' behavior leads to unhandled promise rejections, race conditions, and incomplete cleanup, as surrounding try-catch blocks cannot properly handle errors from these unawaited promises. Replace forEach with for...of loops or Promise.all() with map() to ensure proper sequential execution and error handling.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Async forEach does not await calendar/video deletions

bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => ...) starts asynchronous getCalendar/deleteEvent/deleteMeeting operations, but Array.prototype.forEach does not wait for the callbacks' promises. The surrounding try/catch will not catch rejections, and Reschedule can send the reschedule email and return before the external events are deleted. Use Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(...)) or a for...of loop with await.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments flag forEach with async callbacks that are never awaited, which affects the calendar/video deletions. Both note that try/catch cannot catch the rejections and both recommend Promise.all with map or a for...of loop. The issue is the same.

false_positives.candidate:
All app-store imports are started eagerly, not lazily

The appStore object initializes every entry with import(...) at module load. Importing appStore therefore starts loading every app chunk, even if only one integration is used. This defeats much of the benefit of async imports and can increase startup/network cost. It also creates many promises that may never be awaited; if one dynamic import fails and that app is never used, the rejection may become unhandled. A lazy getter or function that imports only the requested app would be safer.

Reschedule mutation fires calendar/video deletions without awaiting them

bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => ...) performs awaited getCalendar and returns deleteEvent/deleteMeeting promises, but forEach ignores those promises. The mutation can complete, send emails, and call webhooks before external calendar/video events are deleted, and any deletion failure becomes an unhandled promise rejection. Use Promise.all or a for...of loop and await the deletions.

Async forEach can leave apiDeletes unpopulated and unawaited

The recurring-calendar cancellation branch uses .forEach(async (credential) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(...); ... apiDeletes.push(...) }). Because forEach does not await async callbacks, later code may reach await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes)) before apiDeletes is fully populated, so calendar deletions may not be awaited or may be skipped. Errors from those async callbacks are also unhandled. Use a for...of loop or collect promises with map and Promise.all.

Awaiting the apiDeletes array does not await its promises

In the paid cancellation path, await apiDeletes; awaits the array object, not the promises it may contain. The handler can return before calendar/video deletion promises settle, and rejections from those promises may become unhandled. It should be await Promise.all(apiDeletes), after ensuring apiDeletes is fully populated.
